Compares VERA4cast forecast skill (CRPS) between FLARE (daily data assimilation) and a climatology null model at site `fcre`.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
```

## Load data

Public, anonymous-access parquet archive of VERA4cast forecast scores, read directly from S3/OSN without downloading.

```{r}
all_results <- arrow::open_dataset("s3://anonymous@bio230121-bucket01/vera4cast/scores/bundled-parquet/project_id=vera4cast?endpoint_override=amnh1.osn.mghpcc.org")
df <- all_results |>
  dplyr::filter(model_id %in% c("climatology", "glm_aed_flare_v3"),
         variable %in% c("Temp_C_mean", "Chla_ugL_mean", "Secchi_m_sample", "DO_mgL_mean"),
         site_id == "fcre") |>
  dplyr::collect()
```

## Clean and pair forecasts

Relabels variables/models for plotting (newlines in `model_id` keep facet/legend labels compact), computes forecast horizon in days, and restricts to horizons of 30 days or less. Pivoting wide then back to long drops rows without a score from *both* models, giving a fair paired comparison at every horizon/variable.

```{r}
cleaned_df <- df  |>
  mutate(variable = fct_relevel(variable, "Temp_C_mean", "DO_mgL_mean", "Chla_ugL_mean", "Secchi_m_sample"),
         variable = fct_recode(variable,
                       "Water temperature (°C)" = "Temp_C_mean",
                       "Dissolved oxygen (mg/L)" = "DO_mgL_mean",
                        "Chlorophyll-a (μg/L)" = "Chla_ugL_mean",
                        "Secchi depth (m)" = "Secchi_m_sample"),
         model_id = ifelse(model_id == "glm_aed_flare_v3", "FLARE\ndaily data\nassimilation", "climatology\nnull\n")) |>
  mutate(horizon = as.numeric(datetime - reference_datetime) / (60*60*24)) |>
  filter(horizon <= 30) |>
  select(model_id, reference_datetime, horizon, crps, variable) |>
  group_by(model_id, reference_datetime, horizon, variable) |>
  slice(1) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = model_id, values_from = crps) |>
  filter(!is.na(`FLARE\ndaily data\nassimilation`) & !is.na(`climatology\nnull\n`)) |>
  pivot_longer(4:5, names_to = "model_id", values_to = "crps") |>
  ungroup()
```

## Summarize

Summarize by horizon for each model and variable

```{r}
summary_df <-  cleaned_df |>
  group_by(model_id, horizon, variable) |>
  summarize(mean_crps = mean(crps, na.rm = TRUE),
            n = n())
```

Max sample size backing any `mean_crps` value.

```{r}
summary_df |>
  ungroup() |>
  summarise(max = max(n))
```

Date range of `reference_datetime` covered by the paired data.

```{r}
cleaned_df |>
  summarize(min = min(reference_datetime),
            max = max(reference_datetime))
```

## Skill comparison

For each variable, the longest horizon at which FLARE still beats climatology on average (lower CRPS = better forecast skill).

```{r}
summary_df |>
  select(-n) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = model_id, values_from = mean_crps) |>
  mutate(FLARE_better = ifelse(`FLARE\ndaily data\nassimilation` < `climatology\nnull\n`, 1, 0)) |>
  filter(FLARE_better == 1) |>
  group_by(variable) |>
  summarize(max = max(horizon))
```

## Figure 3

Mean CRPS vs. forecast horizon, one facet per variable.

```{r}
p <- summary_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = horizon, y = mean_crps, color = model_id)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~variable, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = "Days in future", y = "Mean Continuous Ranked Probability Score", color = "Model type") +
  theme_bw()

p

ggsave("figure_3.png", p, width = 6, height = 4, dpi = 300)
```
